newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mixed midday, PGMs still higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mixed midday, PGMs still higher.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures were mixed midday, but NYMEX platinum group metals (PGMs) remained sharply higher, with palladium futures locked limit up in the first three contracts out to March 1998.

"Palladium is limit bid and is leading platinum higher as the Russian just don't appear to be shipping much and spot palladium jumped $12.00 an ounce overnight," NYMEX floor trader and RJ Futures president Ralph D'Esposito said.
NYMEX September palladium was up $6.00 at $206.60 an ounce, a new contract high, with the December 1997 and March 1998 contracts also limit bid at new contract highs.
The September/December backwardation remained around $8.00 an ounce, while the platinum/palladium spread in the spot market remained around $215.00 an ounce.
Palladium went limit up for the third day in a row on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) overnight also, on heavy broker shortcovering, traders said.

Spot palladium was quoted $221.60/224.60 an ounce, its highest levels since a 17 year high was seen in June around $240.00, while one month palladium lease rates were still around 75 percent, refining sources said.

NYMEX October platinum was up $9.50 at $435.00 an ounce, after seeing a new contract high at $436.50 early. The October/January backwardation was steady around $13.00 an ounce, with new contract highs were also seen in the January 1998 and April 1998 contracts.

The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread soared to new contract highs at $109.10 an ounce, and the platinum/gold spread in the spot market looked to be heading back towards levels last seen in the 1980's, analysts said.
Spot platinum quoted $437.00/440.00, its highest levels since a seven year high around $500.00 was seen in June, and one month platinum lease rates around 30 percent.

No further Russian shipments of platinum group metals (PGMs) are expected in Japan under the annual supply contract until at least August 6, and offerings earlier this week by Russia in the spot market of parcels of only about 15,000 ounces of platinum are not meeting demand, traders said.
Russian exports of PGMs resumed in July after a six months suspension. Russia supplies about 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium.

Meanwhile, South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) said Friday all workers at its platinum refineries had reported for work desite the National Union of Mineworkers notice of a strike on Thursday. South Africa supplies about 690 percent of the world's platinum and about 20 percent of its palladium.
COMEX September silver was down 2.0 cents at $4.447 an ounce, giving back some of Thursday's sharp gains, after a breakout from a three week old range between $4.20 and $4.40.

"Some people see a gap on the charts from $4.55 to $4.56, and one fund has been a very heavy buyer the last two days and maybe looking to fill gap, but a weak gold price is dragging silver back down and I'm a scale up seller," COMEX floor trader and Rosko Futures president John Rosko said.
COMEX December gold was unchanged at $328.60 an ounce midday.

COMEX gold open interest continued to fall Thursday, dropping 3,677 lots to 184,713 contracts, its lowest level in a month, as funds continued to reduc the record net short positions built up in June.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $324.10/60, compared with the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.10 and the New York close Thursday at $324.30/80.

Gold as usual failed to respond to the latest U.S. economic news in which U.S. unemployment fell to 4.8 percent, its lowest level in nearly a quarter of a century, and June personal income rose 0.6 percent and non-farm payrolls rose 316,000 in July.

But U.S. treasury bond yields fell sharply, dragging U.S. stockmarket prices down, after the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) data for July turned out to be much stronger than expected.
